questions.question: What is different about castor seeds?

options.text: It is the only rabi crop
It is neither rabi nor kharif
It is both rabi and kharif crop

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It is __**both rabi and kharif crop.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• ** Castor seeds are a unique crop as they can be grown in both rabi and kharif seasons.**
 
• This means that farmers have the flexibility to cultivate** castor seeds twice a year.**
 
• Castor seeds are also known as non-food oilseed crops.
 
• They are primarily grown for their oil, which is used in a variety of industries such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and lubricants.
 
• Castor seeds require **warm temperatures and well-drained soil to grow.**
 
• They are not suitable for areas with **heavy rainfall or high humidity.**
 
• Castor seeds are also known for their high resistance to pests and diseases. This makes them a low-maintenance crop, which is ideal for small farmers who may not have access to expensive pesticides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rabi crops are those that are sown in the winter and harvested in the spring. Examples of rabi crops include wheat, barley, and mustard.
 
• Kharif crops are those that are sown in the rainy season and harvested in the autumn. Examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, and cotton.
 
• Zaid crops are those that are grown in the summer season between rabi and kharif. Examples of zaid crops include watermelon, cucumber, and bitter gourd.

questions.question: As per the 73rd and 74th amendment India has ______-tier government system
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Three__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Panchayati Raj System -

 
 
• It was first introduced in India by the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on 2 October 1959 in the Nagaur district of Rajasthan.
 
• Panchayati Raj system is the system of local self-government of rural India.
 
• Self-governance of urban areas is carried out by municipalities and sub-municipalities.
 
• Self-governance of rural areas is carried out through Panchayati Raj Institutions.
 
• Panchayati Raj institutions are three -
 
 
• Gram Panchayat at the village level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at Block (Taluka) level
 
• Zilla Parishad at the district level
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• 'Panchayati Raj Day is observed every year on 24 April in India.
 
• In the year 1993, through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in India got constitutional status.
 
• Lord Ripon is considered the father of local self-government in India during the British rule in India.
 
• In the year 1882, he made a proposal regarding local self-government.

questions.question: Jagoi and Cholom are the two main divisions in which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Manipuri is an ancient classical dance form that originated in the northeastern state of Manipur in India.
 
• Jagoi and cholom are the two main divisions in Manipur’s dance, the one gentle and the other vigorous, corresponding to the lasya and tandava elements described in Sanskrit literature.
 
• There are essentially two divisions in the classical Manipuri dance:
 
 
• Jagoi
 
 
• Predominant in Ras Leela, this steam represents the Lasya element described in Bharata’s Natya Shastra. Here, the legs are generally bent and the knees are kept together. The foot movements are not as loud and pronounced as in the other classical dances of India.
 
 
 
• Cholom
 
 
• ​This represents the Tandava form of classical dance

questions.question: Which of the following major incidents occurred in 1919?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 (on the day of Baisakhi).
 
• It took place at Jallianwala Bagh near the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab province of India.
 
• A large peaceful crowd had gathered to protest against the Rowlatt Act 
 
• An English officer named General Dyer blocked the exit with his troops and ordered them to shoot at the crowd, continuing to fire even as the protestors tried to flee.
 
• In the massacre, more than 400 people died and more than 2000 were injured.
 
• This incident shocked Rabindranath Tagore to such an extent that he renounced his knighthood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__** **____**Bengal partition:**__

• And was implemented on 16 October 1905
 
• However, in 1911 it was withdrawn by Lord Hardinge.
 
 

**Non-cooperation movement:**__

__
 
• The Non-cooperation Movement started in 1920.
 
• The leader of the Non-Cooperation Movement was Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The non-cooperation movement was a mass movement that involved participation from the nationalists as well as the public. 

**Champaran movements**__

 
• Champaran Satyagraha was Mahatma Gandhi’s first experiment of Satyagraha.
 
• It was undertaken in the erstwhile undivided Champaran district in northern Bihar in April 1917.
 
• It was undertaken after Mahatma Gandhi learned about the abuses suffered by farmers, who were forced into growing indigo by British planters and estate owners.

questions.question: The sound waves having frequencies less than ________ Hz are called infrasonic waves
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __20__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves and frequency can be defined as the number of wave cycles happening in one sec.
 
• The types of sound waves whose frequencies are lower than the audible limit of human hearing are called Infrasonic waves.
 
 
• Frequencies less than 20 Hz.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Frequency can be divided into three categories based on their frequency range:

 
 
• ​Audible sound waves: The frequency range of this wave is 20Hz - 20000Hz. Humans can easily detect these types of waves.
 
• Example: Sound produced by Vocal cords.
 
• Infrasonic waves: The frequency range of these types of waves is below 20Hz. Humans cannot detect it. 
 
• Example: Sound produced by Earthquake, Volcanic eruption and ocean waves, etc.
 
• Ultrasonic waves or Ultrasound waves: The sound frequency above 20,000Hz is known as ultrasonic waves. Humans cannot detect it too.

questions.question: In plants cell, ______ are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Leucoplasts__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Leucoplasts are present in plant cells, located in tissues such as roots, bulbs, and seeds. They are plastids category but colourless (non-pigment) as compared to the other plastids like chloroplast.
 
• Chromoplast is a plastid which contains a pigment called lycopeneconsists (red, yellow and orange coloured pigments). It is present in the lumina of membrane sacs as a form of crystals.
 
• A chloroplast (a type of plastid) is an organelle within the green plant cell and certain algae that is the site of the photosynthesis process. It contains chlorophyll to absorb light energy. Chloroplasts have small circular chromosomes known as extranuclear DNA.
 
• Chromatophores, pigment-containing and light-reflecting cell in the deeper layers of the skin of animals. It is the cause of changes in colour or brightness in the organism. chromatophores are termed melanophores (black), erythrophores (red), xanthophores (yellow), or leucophores (white). The distribution of the chromatophores and the pigments they contain determine the colour patterns of an organism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Mitochondria:**

 
• Mitochondria is is a double-layered cell organelle, in which the outer layer is porous and the inner layer is folded upon itself is known to be cristae.
 
• The number of mitochondria in a single cell may be up to 50 to 5000.
 
• The inner lumen of mitochondria contains ribosome phosphate particles and DNA molecules.
 
• It has the potential to synthesize its own protein and the oxidation of carbohydrates and fats takes place with the help of enzymes in mitochondria.
 
• This energy is stored in the form of ATP ( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the "Powerhouse of the cell".

Vacuoles are large membrane sacs found in the cytoplasm.
These store substances that are not essentially useful for the cell (like water, sap, excretory products, and other materials).

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is named only once in Rigveda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Ganga.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rigveda is one of the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, composed in the ancient Sanskrit language.**
 
• It contains hymns and prayers dedicated to various deities and natural elements like rivers, mountains, and forests.
 
• **Among the rivers mentioned in Rigveda, Ganga is the only one that is named just once, in the 10th book, hymn 75, verse 5.**
 
• Indus, Saraswati, and Jhelum are also mentioned in Rigveda, but multiple times, indicating their significance in the ancient Indian civilization.
 
• Ganga is considered a sacred river in Hinduism and is worshipped as a goddess. It is also the largest river in India, flowing through several states and supporting millions of people for their livelihood. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Indus is one of the oldest and longest rivers in Asia, flowing through India, Pakistan, and China. It was the cradle of the Indus Valley Civilization, one of the earliest urban civilizations in the world.
 
• Saraswati is a mythical river that is believed to have flown in ancient India but dried up due to geological changes. It is considered a goddess of learning, wisdom, and music in Hinduism.
 
• Jhelum is a river that flows through the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir and the Pakistani province of Punjab. It was known as Hydaspes in ancient times and was the site of the famous battle between Alexander the Great and King Porus in 326 BCE.
